request.prompt:
# Task
Design the system for `spec.json` and plan the work. Technology constraints: C# on .NET 10, ASP.NET Core minimal APIs, Entity Framework Core with SQLite for storage, xUnit with Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing (WebApplicationFactory) for tests. Layout: the API project is src/App/App.csproj with Program.cs ending in `public partial class Program { }` so tests can host it; the test project is tests/Tests.csproj with a ProjectReference to ../src/App/App.csproj. Nullable reference types enabled. Configuration from appsettings.json and environment variables; never hard-code secrets. NuGet packages allowed: Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.InMemory, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design, Microsoft.Data.Sqlite (API); Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, xunit, xunit.runner.visualstudio, coverlet.collector, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing (tests).
- components: one per C# file or project, with its file path (for example src/App/Services/LinkService.cs).
- api: every endpoint with method, path, status codes and the requirement ids it serves.
- data_model; decisions (D1, ...) with rationale and rejected alternatives; risks with mitigations.
- tasks (T1, ...): small, each owned by developer, tester or docs, citing requirement ids, sequenced with
  depends_on. Every 'must' requirement needs at least one task.
- Tests and docs are written in parallel with the code from this design (contract-first), so pin file
  paths, type and method names, request/response shapes and the API precisely.

# Inputs

## spec.json
{
  "title": "URL Shortener Service Requirements Specification",
  "problem_statement": "Provide a robust, secure, and persistent HTTP URL shortener service that allows users to create shortened links (with auto-generated codes or custom aliases and optional expiry), redirects callers to the original target while tracking click metrics, provides health checks, and protects against SSRF and abuse.",
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "R1",
      "text": "The service must provide an endpoint to shorten a target URL using an auto-generated unique code.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "POST /shorten with body {\"url\": \"https://example.com/very/long/path\"} returns HTTP 201 with body containing a generated string 'code' and full 'short_url'.",
        "Subsequent requests with different URLs receive distinct, non-colliding generated codes."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R2",
      "text": "The service must allow clients to specify a custom unique alias during link creation and reject duplicates.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "POST /shorten with body {\"url\": \"https://example.com\", \"custom_alias\": \"my-link\"} returns HTTP 201 with code 'my-link'.",
        "POST /shorten with body {\"url\": \"https://other.com\", \"custom_alias\": \"my-link\"} when 'my-link' already exists returns HTTP 409 Conflict with an error message indicating the alias is already in use."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R3",
      "text": "The service must redirect requests for valid short codes to the original target URL and increment the link's click count.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "GET /{code} for an active code redirects to the original target URL with HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect and Location header matching the target URL.",
        "GET /{code} for a non-existent code returns HTTP 404 Not Found.",
        "Each successful GET /{code} increases total click count by 1 and updates last_visited_at to the current timestamp."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R4",
      "text": "The service must support optional expiration for links and reject redirection once expired.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "POST /shorten with {\"url\": \"https://example.com\", \"expires_at\": \"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\"} stores the expiration timestamp.",
        "GET /{code} executed after the specified expiration timestamp returns HTTP 404 Not Found and does not increment click count."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R5",
      "text": "The service must provide an analytics endpoint returning total clicks, creation timestamp, and last visited timestamp for a code.",
      "category": "functional",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "GET /analytics/{code} for a newly created link with 0 visits returns HTTP 200 with {\"total_clicks\": 0, \"created_at\": \"<ISO-8601>\", \"last_visited_at\": null}.",
        "GET /analytics/{code} following a visit returns HTTP 200 with updated 'total_clicks' count and an ISO-8601 'last_visited_at' timestamp.",
        "GET /analytics/{code} for a non-existent code returns HTTP 404 Not Found."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R6",
      "text": "The service must expose a health check endpoint for load balancers indicating operational status.",
      "category": "reliability",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "GET /health when database and service are operational returns HTTP 200 OK with body {\"status\": \"healthy\"}.",
        "GET /health when backing datastore is unavailable returns HTTP 503 Service Unavailable."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R7",
      "text": "The service must prevent SSRF and unsafe protocols by strictly validating target URLs before shortening.",
      "category": "security",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "POST /shorten with URL using non-HTTP(S) scheme (e.g., 'ftp://example.com', 'javascript:alert(1)') returns HTTP 400 Bad Request.",
        "POST /shorten with target resolving to loopback or private IP ranges (e.g., 'http://localhost', 'http://127.0.0.1:8080', 'http://169.254.169.254', 'http://10.0.0.1', 'http://[::1]') returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with an SSRF prevention error.",
        "POST /shorten with a public domain that resolves to a private IP address returns HTTP 400 Bad Request."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R8",
      "text": "The service must enforce per-client rate limiting on link creation to mitigate spam and denial of service.",
      "category": "security",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Exceeding the configured threshold of POST /shorten calls from a single client IP within a rate-limit window returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header.",
        "Requests within the allowed rate limit window succeed with HTTP 201."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R9",
      "text": "The service must persist all shortened URLs, metadata, and analytics data across application restarts.",
      "category": "reliability",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Create link 'abc' via POST /shorten, stop the service process, restart the service, and verify GET /abc returns HTTP 307 and GET /analytics/abc returns previous click history."
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "R10",
      "text": "The service codebase must provide comprehensive automated tests and clear documentation.",
      "category": "usability",
      "priority": "must",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Running the test suite executes automated tests covering all endpoints (POST /shorten, GET /{code}, GET /analytics/{code}, GET /health) including success, validation errors, expired links, and rate limits.",
        "A README.md exists in repository root detailing environment setup, execution commands, testing commands, and endpoint API contract documentation."
      ]
    }
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect is used instead of HTTP 301 Permanent Redirect so that user-agents do not cache the redirection locally, ensuring every click hits the server for analytics tracking.",
    "Client identity for rate-limiting is determined by client remote IP or a validated 'X-Forwarded-For' header when behind a trusted reverse proxy.",
    "Generated short codes use Base62 alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9) with a default minimum length of 7 characters.",
    "Custom aliases are constrained to alphanumeric characters, dashes, and underscores with length between 3 and 64 characters.",
    "Database storage uses an embedded or network SQL/key-value store persisting to disk to fulfill restart survivability."
  ],
  "open_questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "question": "Should GET /{code} return HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect or HTTP 301 Permanent Redirect?",
      "why_it_matters": "HTTP 301 is aggressively cached by browsers, preventing repeat visits by the same client from hitting the server and undercounting analytics.",
      "blocking": true,
      "proposed_default": "Use HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect to ensure all visits are tracked in analytics."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "question": "What schema and format should be used for link expiration in the POST /shorten request payload?",
      "why_it_matters": "Determines request payload validation, serialization, and whether clients supply an absolute timestamp (e.g., ISO 8601) or a relative TTL in seconds.",
      "blocking": true,
      "proposed_default": "Accept an optional ISO-8601 UTC timestamp string in field 'expires_at'."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "question": "What is the exact rate limit policy (capacity and window) for POST /shorten per client IP?",
      "why_it_matters": "Directly affects client experience, load testing thresholds, and security bounds.",
      "blocking": false,
      "proposed_default": "Limit to 60 requests per minute per IP address."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "question": "Should expired links retain their analytics or be purged, and can an expired custom alias be reclaimed?",
      "why_it_matters": "Affects data retention policies, GET /analytics behavior on expired codes, and unique constraint indexing.",
      "blocking": true,
      "proposed_default": "Retain expired link records for analytics access (GET /analytics/{code} still accessible with an 'expired': true flag), and prevent alias reuse to avoid link hijacking."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope": [
    "User registration, authentication, API keys, or role-based access control.",
    "Editing target URLs or manual deletion of created short links.",
    "Advanced analytics dimensions such as referrer tracking, geolocation, user-agent parsing, or timeseries click graphs.",
    "Custom branded domains or DNS configuration management.",
    "Web frontend or UI dashboard."
  ]
}

request.system: You are a pragmatic software architect and tech lead. You design the simplest architecture that meets the requirements, record decisions with the alternatives you rejected, and break the work into small, traceable tasks.
